name: treewalk
axis: recursion over a REAL recursive heap structure — pointer-chasing binary tree, built recursively then walked recursively
notes: A perfect binary tree of depth 19 (1_048_575 nodes, ~32MB of heap) built by `build` and summed by `sum`, 150 times. Recursion depth is only 20, so CPython runs it under its default limit unchanged — only the repeat count is reduced for Python. The root's value is mutated each pass: WITHOUT that, rustc hoisted all 150 walks into one (44ms == build + a single walk) and the benchmark was VOID; the mutation makes the walk not loop-invariant in all four. VERIFIED LINEAR rather than 2x-scaled, because the one-time tree build is a fixed cost that a naive N/2N ratio misreads (deno's raw 150->300 ratio is 1.56 for exactly that reason). Measured at 1, 150 and 300 walks, the INCREMENTAL cost per walk is constant: rust 5.13ms then 4.50ms, vl 4.74ms then 5.24ms, deno 7.15ms then 7.52ms — nothing folded or cached. Interleaved min-of-2 on core 6: rust 0.802s, vl 0.764s, deno 1.141s; python(20 walks) 3.004s. VL ESSENTIALLY TIES RUST here (0.95x) and is 1.49x faster than deno — the best VL result in this category, and evidence that WasmGC struct field loads plus null-narrowing cost about what a Rust Option<Box<T>> deref costs. Build-only cost (t at 1 walk): rust 0.038s, vl 0.057s, deno 0.076s, python 1.30s — CPython spends ~43% of its total on building 1M objects.
vlNote: No opt.vl: the idiomatic spelling already matches rust. `t.left != null` narrowing inside the recursion emitted clean code and needed no hint.

startupBaselineSeconds._measured: min-of-10, empty program, taskset -c 6, contended 24-core i9-12900KF

compileTime._note: compile time, measured separately and never inside an execution number

consolidatedRun._method: single interleaved pass over ALL 8 recursion benchmarks, min-of-3, taskset -c 6, per-runtime empty-program startup subtracted, machine contended by other agents (loadavg ~10) so read the RATIOS not the absolutes

audit.pythonNormalisationIsNotAMultiply: Python runs 20 walks vs 150, but its wall time is dominated by the ONE-TIME 1M-node tree build, so multiplying by 7.5 is wrong. Independently measured 150->75 walks: rust 1.97x, deno 2.30x, VL 1.86x, python(20->10) 1.18x. Naive 7.5x normalisation gives 21.4s; the honest extrapolation from the note's own build-only figure is ~8.4s. Use incremental-cost-per-walk, not total x 7.5.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
